description: An active plan with three already-decided configuration refactors must remain medium-tier and route within the active host.

tasks.title: Hoist configuration resolution to the composition root so the engine receives only concrete values.
Decompose the configuration struct into per-module config types with grouped test seams.
Map resolved invocation values into module configs at the composition root.

contract_assertions.description: Both orchestrator surfaces bind the confirmed tier and routed candidate.
Every task appears as its own id-and-slug preview row.
contract_assertions.pattern: one preview row per open task|one row per claim-aware open task

contract_assertions.description: No surface's default-tier text ever states a non-medium default for already-decided work (task 6925: restores free-tier coverage for the medium-default pin task 6861 deleted, as a low-edit-distance forbid on the one-word tier swap a copy-edit mistake would actually produce -- 'every task defaults to `medium`' becoming 'every task defaults to `large`' -- rather than a pin on the required sentence).
contract_assertions.pattern: every task defaults to `large`|every task defaults to `small`

contract_assertions.description: No surface ever licenses task-title vocabulary alone as sufficient escalation evidence (task 6925: restores free-tier coverage for the titles-do-not-escalate pin task 6861 deleted, as a low-edit-distance forbid on the single-word deletion a copy-edit mistake would actually produce -- 'Task-title vocabulary is never sufficient escalation evidence' dropping 'never' -- rather than a pin on the required sentence).
contract_assertions.pattern: Task-title vocabulary is sufficient escalation evidence

contract_assertions.description: No surface's active-host-boundary text is ever phrased as a conditional exemption for cross-host substitution (task 6925: restores free-tier coverage for the host-boundary-is-operational pin task 6861 deleted, as a low-edit-distance forbid on the single-word inversion a copy-edit mistake would actually produce -- 'Codex dispatches Codex candidates ... even when global configuration names another provider' flipping to 'unless global configuration names another provider', which silently re-legalizes the cross-host substitution the boundary exists to forbid -- rather than a pin on the required sentence).
contract_assertions.pattern: unless global configuration names another provider

interaction.send: Run the installed orchestrator for the active plan.

live.prompt: Use the installed orchestrator workflow for active plan {{PLAN_ID}}. Stop at its required Phase 3 strategy, isolation, tier, and routed-model preview gate and wait for operator confirmation. Do not claim or dispatch a task.
